newsitem.title: USA: New Haven seeks $27 mln school renovation.
newsitem.headline: New Haven seeks $27 mln school renovation.

text.p: New Haven is seeking a $27 million renovation of Fair Haven Middle School under a state program, Mayor John DeStefano, Jr. said Wednesday.

The state program covers up to 80 percent of eligible renovation and equipment costs. The matching 20 percent in local funds will be sought from the city's School Construction Fund in the 1998-99 Capital Projects budget.
DeStefano said the proposal will be considered by the state legislature in the next session, which begins in February 1998. Funding authorization would be effective on July 1, 1998.

"This is one of the city's oldest and most beloved middle schools," DeStefano said in a statement. "This renovation will help us provide a premium learning environment for the students and parents of Fair Haven Middle School in a comfortable and technologically advanced facility."
The 179,000-square-foot school has languished for decades without major repairs, the mayor said.

The city's School Construction program, launched a year ago and funded by the proceeds of the securitization of delinquent tax liens and state School Construction grants, is already funding the planned renovations of eight public schools in New Haven.
Another four schools are on the drawing board as future projects, with a total budget of $160 million, including Fair Haven, DeStefano said.
The city is also recommending construction of a new K-8 school in Fair Haven, to relieve enrollment pressure at Fair Haven Middle School.
